_comment: The DB-ESDK TestServer Configuration_Set (design 'Data Models'): exactly
one product field, exactly one Feature_Catalog (the features list,
Requirement 7.1), and one Configuration_Entry per language (Requirements
Languages: Java, Rust, .NET — each hosted in its own sibling
Language_Repository (aws-crypto-tools-java, aws-crypto-tools-rust,
aws-crypto-tools-dotnet). Each server wraps its language's published DBE
distribution behind the same rpcv2Cbor wire contract, so the generated
Java Test_Client talks to any of them and TamperTest / DbeAwsKmsRoundTripTest
iterate every (encrypt, decrypt) pair automatically.
Feature_Catalog: 'raw-aes' and 'aws-kms', both backed by real cross-
language Tests. Each declared Feature must be supported by every launched
Language_Server for the test matrix to be sensible; adding a Feature
requires every language wrapper to expose it. The Java DBE library in
fact supports every keyring the MPL exposes; entries are added to the
catalog once all three wrappers ship the corresponding Test coverage.
Branch pins: while each DBE test-server host branch is unmerged, the
entries pin the working-branch on their host repo. The workingTreeOverlay.*
args the Makefile passes redirect the SourceResolver to the sibling
checkout, so the branch pin is a documentation contract for reproducible
runs after those branches merge — not a runtime constraint today.
.NET blocker: the aws/aws-crypto-tools-dotnet host repository does not
yet exist on GitHub (as of this commit, `git ls-remote` returns
'repository not found'). The .NET Language_Server code is local-only in
sibling checkouts and reaches the orchestrator via workingTreeOverlay, so
make orchestrate runs fine locally. Reproducible runs from a fresh clone
will remain blocked on the .NET entry until the repo is created and the
server tree pushed to huaye/dbesdk-test-server there.
